official_finding.summary: Before dawn on 28 January 2017, the outbound oil tanker MT Dawn Kanchipuram and the inbound LPG tanker MT BW Maple collided in the approach channel off Kamarajar (Ennore) Port, north of Chennai. Bunker/fuel oil released from Dawn Kanchipuram drifted south and heavily oiled Chennai's northern shoreline (Ernavur, Thiruvottiyur) and later the Marina. The initial official spill estimate was very low (order of 1 tonne) and was revised upward repeatedly over the following days; independent assessments put the release at a substantially larger figure. INCOIS issued oil-spill drift forecasts to the Indian Coast Guard during the response.

official_finding.caveat: There is no SAR-visible slick in the 29 Jan 2017 Sentinel-1 dawn pass — sheltered water, low wind. This is a known-source case: the origin is the documented collision position in the Kamarajar Port approach channel, not a NAAP detection. There is no attribution act because Indian coastal AIS is not publicly available in bulk — so NAAP cannot independently place either vessel, and we say so.
